slice: sensor reading scoped audit and caller-owned transaction
verified: Successful manual sensor-reading audits receive the same database connection and canonical location ID as the reading insert.
Manual and CSV EventBus writes use commit=False so the caller owns the transaction.
CSV row savepoints preserve prior accepted rows when a later row fails and is audited.
A synthetic two-row batch proves a failed second row does not globally roll back the first accepted row.
Standalone and unified successful manual-reading commands produce identical output and the same scoped transactional effects.
Rejected readings create a location-scoped failure audit, commit that audit, and do not insert a sensor reading.
Unknown sensors create a fixed-message location-scoped failure audit without echoing the supplied sensor identifier in logs.
An outbox/event enqueue failure rolls back the reading and its previously inserted success audit and closes the connection.
external_effects: Database, ClickHouse, and EventBus calls were mocked. No database, provider, or candidate service was contacted.
limitations: No live PostgreSQL transaction or tenant authorization was exercised.
No populated sensor-device or reading fixture was compared.
